title: Set the font size and turn on bold text in Settings

setup.why: Keep the phone's own font scale and weight once (a retried setup keeps the first copy), so teardown puts them back.

argv: f=/data/local/tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}}.orig; [ -e $f ] || { echo "system font_scale $(settings get system font_scale)"; echo "secure font_weight_adjustment $(settings get secure font_weight_adjustment)"; } > $f

setup.why: Start two font-size steps away from the asked size, with bold text off.

argv: settings put system font_scale {{x.start}} && settings put secure font_weight_adjustment 0

setup.why: Open Settings at its home page, whatever screen an earlier run left it on.

instruction: Using the Settings app, set the font size to {{x.say}} and turn on bold text. Leave the display size as it is.

checks.why: Prints system/font_scale, then secure/font_weight_adjustment. Font size {{x.say}} is a font_scale of {{x.say}} / 100; bold text on is a weight adjustment of 300. Setup left {{x.start}} and 0, so an agent that does nothing fails.
argv: echo "$(settings get system font_scale) $(settings get secure font_weight_adjustment)"

teardown.why: Put the phone's own font scale and weight back (deleted when it had none), and drop the saved copy.

oracle.why: Wait for Settings' window: on a fresh phone it shows a moment after am start -W returns.

Every size is one step from where setup left it: a press re-renders the button, so a second press in the same act would hold a stale ref, and the "Font size added to Quick Settings" popup the first press shows would cover a second act's look.
